entries.title: Guilds can now post dungeon runs and guild events.
entries.html: Officers can now post dungeon runs and guild events as well as raids. Members sign up the same way.

entries.title: Raid sign-ups show spec, class and a class count.
entries.html: Sign-ups now show spec and class, a class count for buffs, and Melee and Ranged like the Discord post. Times read in the guild’s clock first.

entries.title: World of Warcraft: Forever launched.
entries.html: World of Warcraft: Forever launched on 4 Nov 2026 at 3 pm PST. Invite-a-Friend launch week access runs from 4 to 11 Nov.

entries.title: Premium log coach: the casts, buffs and consumables to fix first.
entries.html: Added the log coach for Premium. After every logged raid it tells you what to fix first: the casts you missed, the buffs you let drop and the consumables you skipped, learned from the engine and from the top logs on the site. It reviews every spec; damage specs get the most findings.

entries.title: Raid sign-up buttons and slash commands in your guild Discord.
entries.html: Added the Forever Sixty Discord bot. Raid posts carry In, Late, Bench and Out buttons, and /raid, /bis, /char and more answer in your guild’s Discord. Officers add it from guild settings; members link Discord on the account page.

entries.title: Raid pages now show who came and how the night went.
entries.html: Added attendance and raid-night reports. A raid’s log is matched when it is uploaded, and the raid page shows who came, kill times, deaths, loot and the biggest changes since last time.

entries.title: Guilds can now plan raids, and members sign up on the raid page.
entries.html: Added raid sign-ups. Officers plan raids on the guild’s Raids tab and members sign up from the raid page or the guild page.

entries.title: Premium, Guild and Raid guild: the launch plans and founder prices.
entries.html: Premium is $6 a month or $50 a year, one price for everyone. Guilds pick Guild, $15 a month or $150 a year for up to 25 verified members with one Premium seat, or Raid guild, $25 a month or $250 a year for any size with three seats, the loot council helper, the readiness board and consumables. Officers give seats to any verified member and can move each one once every 30 days. A guild’s first 7 days are free. Subscribe before 6 Jan 2027 and you keep the founder price. A guild’s history is never locked: a lapsed plan keeps its raids and logs readable and downloadable, and the plan can be handed to another officer.

entries.title: Officer tools are now part of the guild plan.
entries.html:
Award and Undo on the loot council helper and Nudge on the raid readiness board are part of the guild plan. Every guild claimed before today keeps them through the first raid nights, until 12 Dec.

The guild settings page shows what your guild has and until when. An officer of a guild without the plan sees the tools read-only, with a sentence saying how to subscribe.

entries.title: Premium members can now see their score and parses over time on their character page.
entries.html:
Premium members now see a History section on their own character page, between the Forever Score card and Gear. Score over time draws each day’s last rated fight as a dated point on the tier bands, with a labelled gap wherever no fight was rated, and lists the fights behind the selected point. Parse by boss draws the parse of every kill of a boss you pick, with its kills listed underneath. The section includes your private and guild reports, and only you see it.

Free members and visitors keep the sparkline on the Forever Score card, and a free owner sees one line pointing to the plans. The account page’s History row now reads Open on your main character for Premium members and Sparkline only for everyone else.

entries.title: Premium members can now get a Discord message when a server sim or a log upload finishes.
entries.html:
Added Discord notifications. Premium members can paste a Discord webhook on the account page and get a message when a server sim finishes or a log finishes parsing. Pick which of the two you want, and send a test message to see it arrive. The link is encrypted and never shown again; the page shows the webhook’s own name (the one you gave it in Discord) and the channel’s id.

If Discord refuses five posts in a row, the messages switch off and the account page says why. Fix the channel, press Test and switch on, and they resume. If your plan ends, your webhook is kept and posts start again when you are back on Premium. You can remove the webhook at any time. Free members see one line pointing to the plans, and the Premium rows on the account page now show whether Discord messages are on.

Private logs are your choice. New webhooks leave them off; a webhook saved before today keeps posting them until you untick Include private logs on the account page. You can also connect a channel from the account page: pick the server and channel in Discord and the webhook is made for you, with the paste form still there if you prefer it.

entries.title: The Premium page now lists only what is live, and logs are kept for everyone.
entries.html:
The Premium page now lists only what is live today, with the month beside what is coming: character history charts are marked November and Discord notifications December. The guild plan’s officer tools read as the loot council helper and the raid readiness board, with more as they ship.

Uploaded logs, the reports parsed from them and saved sims are kept for everyone, with no retention tier on any plan. The terms and the privacy policy now say the same, and the FAQ entry about long-retention logs is gone. The line about comparing more than two builds is retired.

entries.title: Server sims keep going after you close the tab, and the site tells you when they finish.
entries.html:
Premium members now see their server runs at the top of the Simulator: each run’s name, spec and state, with an estimate for a running one drawn from the last ten finished runs of that spec, the result for a finished one, and the plain reason for a failed one with a Run again button. Runs start the moment they are sent, so there is no queue and nothing to cancel.

A run that finishes while no tab is open is announced once in the character band on the next page load, with a link to the result. Opening the result or dismissing the line clears it. The account page’s Server sims row now counts this month’s runs.

entries.title: Blizzard moves the Forever stress test to 21 Oct, open to everyone.
entries.html:
Blizzard’s stress test of World of Warcraft: Forever is now on 21 Oct, moved from 19 Oct, and starts at 2 pm PDT in North America (19:00 CEST in Europe). It may end early or run late. The beta is taken offline shortly before it begins and is expected to return shortly after it ends.

When the test ends, every character, name and guild made on the test servers is wiped, ahead of name reservations opening on 27 Oct for pre-purchasers, through 3 Nov.

sources.label: Blizzard, Join the World of Warcraft: Forever Stress Test (updated Oct 16)

entries.title: The simulator now runs Top Gear, Droptimizer, talent compare and stat weights for damage specs.
entries.html:
/sim gained three tools for damage specs, beside the plain run. Top Gear ranks gear and consumable combinations against your current set, one slot or several at once. Droptimizer ranks every drop from the bosses you pick, boss by boss. Talent compare ranks loadouts against each other, your own saved builds included. A fourth tool, stat weights, turns a finished run into the per-point numbers some addons ask for, with the same caution attached everywhere it appears on this site: it holds near the gear you have now and stops holding the moment a set bonus, a proc, or a cap changes. Sim the actual items in Top Gear instead, when you can.

Every tool shares what a plain run already had: fight style, three precision levels, the full buff panel, and the same sample log on /sim. All four run free in the browser; a run past the browser lane’s own cap runs on the server instead, for premium accounts.

Spec support still reads “Not yet” for every damage spec: nothing has been checked against a real parse, because there are no real parses yet. And Droptimizer can only rank what the re-itemised raid tier actually has: a large share of the fork’s own sourced item ids do not exist in the 1.60 client, so a boss can show fewer upgrades than it will once that tier is fully curated.
entries.caveat: Damage specs only, not healers or tanks. Every one of those specs is still "not yet" measured, and raid drops are thin until the re-itemised tier is curated.

entries.title: Blizzard confirms a live developer Q&A on 17 Sep at 10 am PDT.
entries.html:
Blizzard is hosting a live Q&A with members of the World of Warcraft development team on Thursday 17 Sep at 10 am PDT, on the official Warcraft Twitch and YouTube channels, with a VOD afterwards. Questions are collected in a World of Warcraft forum thread.

It is a World of Warcraft Q&A rather than a Forever-only one, and it falls on the same day the beta opens.

sources.label: Blizzard, submit your questions for the 17 Sep live Q&A

entries.title: Two dungeon level ranges revised: City of Dalaran 28 to 30, Krol'dok Stronghold 40 to 55.
entries.html:
A second outlet logged the What’s Next panel live and recorded level ranges off the slides as they appeared. Seven of its nine ranges match the roundup we used on 12 Sep. Two do not.

City of Dalaran is given as levels 28 to 30, where the earlier roundup said roughly 20 to 35. Krol’dok Stronghold is given as levels 40 to 55, where the earlier roundup said 35 to 40; the same log describes it as an outdoor dungeon sitting in the Riverglades zone.

Both figures are single-source either way. We have switched to the panel log, because it records what was on screen at the time.
entries.caveat: Both the old and the new ranges come from a single outlet. Blizzard has never published dungeon level ranges.

sources.label: Output Lag, live log of the What's Next panel

entries.title: Three Forever talent calculators are live, all built from demo footage.
entries.html:
Wowhead, Icy Veins and the fan site talentsforever.com all published Forever talent calculators within two days of the announcement, built from panel slides and BlizzCon demo footage rather than from a game client.

All three come with caveats. Wowhead’s own disclaimer says the data is “mostly” accurate, that talent rank scaling is potentially wrong, and that some new Forever talents have no icons yet; it will be rebuilt from the beta client. talentsforever.com marks which rank values were read verbatim and which are estimated, and publishes its whole dataset under CC BY 4.0.

None of them should be treated as final until the beta client is datamined after 17 Sep.
entries.caveat: Rank scaling in all three calculators is estimated in places.

sources.label: Wowhead, Forever talent calculator now live

entries.title: Talent trees keep seven rows and 51 points, with a new one-point talent at 16.
entries.html:
Talent trees keep the familiar layout: seven rows per tree, 51 points to spend, and the one-point “gold medal” talents at 11, 21 and 31 points. Forever adds a fourth, at the 16-point mark, so every tree has four of them.

Principal Designer Kris Zierhut, in an interview: “We still have what we call them gold medal talents. 11, 21, 31 point, one point talents. Those are all still there. We did add a new one point talent at the 16 point mark.”

Talents that existed mainly to unlock a group buff are becoming baseline abilities instead: Divine Spirit, Blessing of Kings, Improved Mark of the Wild and Improved Battle Shout among them. Some talents are unchanged from 1.12.

entries.title: The Forever beta has a free opt-in; the packs only guarantee a seat.
entries.html:
Blizzard opened a Beta Opt-In button on the Forever page on Battle.net on 13 Sep. Anyone signed in can opt in at no cost, which puts them in the pool without guaranteeing anything.

Guaranteed access still sits with the Skyborne Epic Pack, the Warcraft Forever Collection and the Collector’s Edition. The $29.99 Skyborne Heroic Pack does not include beta access.
entries.caveat: Reported by press coverage of the Battle.net page rather than by a Blizzard news post.

sources.label: Wowhead, opt in for the Forever beta
Insider Gaming, how to access the Forever beta

entries.title: Camping: three objects per campfire, one per player, first learned at skill 20.
entries.html:
A Basic Campfire creates a campsite that gives vendors, repairs, profession workspaces and one-hour buffs. You have to sit for a few moments and become rested before the buffs apply, and some parts of Azeroth are better suited to a quiet rest than others.

Up to three crafted objects can be added to a Basic Campfire, one per player, sharing a one-hour cooldown. Every profession has three objects at different skill levels: a Blacksmith’s Sharpening Wheel raises Attack Power, a Tailor’s Faction Banner raises Spirit, and a Herbalist’s Incense Candle raises Intellect. These are variants of the equivalent class buffs and do not stack with them.

The first objects are learned at profession skill 20, from profession trainers or from camping NPCs; advanced objects come from Blueprint recipes that drop from specific dungeon bosses. Alchemists place an Alchemy Lab, Leatherworkers a Tanning Rack needed for advanced recipes, and Cooks can learn upgraded campfires that hold five or ten objects.

entries.title: Hardcore is coming to Forever after launch, with a safe layer refresh and one-way Legacy.
entries.html:
The Hardcore panel on 13 Sep confirmed Hardcore for Forever but gave no date beyond the roadmap’s “winter.” Production Director Clayton Stone announced it; Senior Game Designer Josh Greenfield covered the history.

A character that dies in Hardcore can transfer to any other ruleset, including PvP and Roleplaying, rather than being forced into PvE as in Classic Hardcore. A new layer-refresh system warns you before a refresh, lets you move somewhere safe and then click a button to trigger it; one outlet reports this applies to every version of the game, not only Hardcore.

Legacy runs one way. You earn Legacy points in Hardcore and each death leaves account-wide bonuses that make the next run easier, and Hardcore will have its own challenges and perks, but points, mounts, pets, appearances and achievements earned outside Hardcore do not carry in. Everything earned inside does carry out.

Greenfield also teased a “dedicated space” for Mak’gora and said the team is thinking about Mak’gora tournaments.
entries.caveat: Blizzard's written recap covers the ruleset and the transfer rule. The layer-refresh system, the one-way Legacy detail and the Mak'gora tease come from panel coverage, not from a Blizzard post.

sources.label: MMO-Champion, The Past, Present, and Future of Hardcore
Warcraft Tavern, Forever was designed with Hardcore in mind

entries.title: Every dungeon drop re-examined; unique boss items are rare quality.
entries.html:
Blizzard says every dungeon drop has been re-examined, hundreds of new drops have been added, unique dungeon boss items are now rare quality, and set bonuses have been improved. Quest rewards were expanded so long questlines stop handing casters two-handed swords: Mor’ladim in Duskwood now also grants the Ladimore Heirloom Ring, and Hemet Nesingwary’s quests add the Master Hunter’s Spellsword.

Trinkets are being pushed toward situational effects, with the Worgenbane Talisman given as an example, and some items now work in specific biomes such as Woodlands, Mountains or Deserts, or against specific creature types. World-drop epics have been improved and hundreds of new rare-creature drops added.

One outlet’s live log of the panel also names the Graverobber’s Shovel and Sharpened Cutlery as new items, plus updated versions of the Tidal Charm and Whitemane’s Chapeau.
entries.caveat: The four item names from the live panel log are reported by one outlet only.

sources.label: PC Gamer, 10 big Forever details from BlizzCon
Output Lag, live log of the What's Next panel

entries.title: Legacy: 65 points earnable at launch, 16 spendable per character, three trees.
entries.html:
Legacy points come from completing challenges while levelling, such as levelling a particular class or profession. Sixty-five are earnable at launch and each character can spend sixteen of them. Points are earned across the account but spent per character, so a Warrior need not pay for a perk that only a caster wants.

The three launch trees are Adventure, Professions and Resourcefulness. Named perks include Well Rested, Bountiful Harvest and Reagent Economy, which removes the vendor reagent cost from class abilities. A separate Legacy Reward Track grants cosmetics such as a Spectral Bear Cub, and mounts are granted when you learn riding. Blizzard says more trees will follow.

The perk list transcribed from the demo runs to twenty entries and includes two Professions slots whose tooltip reads “To be added in future patch content.” It also names a crate turn-in currency called Merchant Favor and two organisations, the Azeroth Commerce Authority and Durotar Supply and Logistics, that Blizzard has not described anywhere.
entries.caveat: The point totals and tree names are Blizzard's. The individual perks, their ranks, and the Merchant Favor crate economy come from one demo transcription.

entries.title: Name reservation covers up to three characters, first come first served.
entries.html: Early Name Reservation, which runs Oct 27 to Nov 3 for anyone who owns an upgrade pack, lets a player create and customise up to three characters to hold their names. It is first come, first served, and Blizzard warns that a desired name is not guaranteed.
entries.caveat: The three-character figure is reported by one outlet and is not in Blizzard's own pre-purchase post.

sources.label: Insider Gaming, how to access the Forever beta

entries.title: Blizzard has not ruled out a new class, correcting announcement-day coverage.
entries.html:
This corrects what we published on 12 Sep. One outlet reported that no new classes were being added. On the What’s Next panel, Associate Production Director Clay Stone said nothing is off the table, not even a new class, next to a fan survey of 35,305 responses in which 42.2 percent wanted no new class and 47.3 percent wanted one in some form.

No new class is in the launch game.
entries.caveat: The survey numbers and the quote come from live coverage of the panel, not from a Blizzard post.

sources.label: Output Lag, live log of the What's Next panel

entries.title: Over 600 new profession recipes; crafted food grants experience.
entries.html: Blizzard says there are over 600 new recipes across professions and level ranges, plus overhauls to existing ones. Fishing and cooking were updated alongside camping, and almost all crafted food now grants a stat boost; Blizzard’s recap adds that crafted food can also grant a small experience bonus.

sources.label: PC Gamer, 10 big Forever details from BlizzCon

entries.title: Every race gets two active and two passive racials; weapon-skill racials now give crit.
entries.html:
Blizzard reworked every race’s abilities so each has two actives and two passives, tuned for similar offensive power. Racials that used to grant Weapon Skill now grant critical strike chance with the matching weapon type, which makes them useful to casters as well as melee.

Blizzard’s own worked examples are Dwarf and Undead. Stoneform now reduces physical damage taken rather than raising armour, Find Treasure stacks with other tracking, Mace Specialization grants crit, and Big Game Hunter adds damage against Beasts. Will of the Forsaken removes Charm, Fear and Sleep but no longer grants immunity, Cannibalize restores mana as well as health, and Touch of the Grave is new.

The numbers for the other seven races come from outlets that played the BlizzCon demo rather than from Blizzard, and they disagree on a few values.
entries.caveat: Blizzard confirmed the structure and the Dwarf and Undead examples. The per-race numbers are demo transcriptions by Icy Veins and Talents Forever, and the two differ on Gnome, Night Elf and Troll values.

entries.title: Forever has no realms. Players pick one of four rulesets instead.
entries.html:
At the Deep Dive panel Blizzard said Forever is realmless. Instead of choosing from a realm list, a player picks one of four rulesets: Normal, where player-versus-player combat requires mutual consent; PvP; Roleplaying; and Hardcore, which arrives after launch.

Each ruleset is a large ecosystem of its own, not one giant realm for everyone. You can only group, run dungeons and raid with players who chose the same ruleset, and Horde and Alliance still cannot group together. Hardcore is fully enclosed, but a Hardcore character that dies can transfer to another ruleset, including PvP.

Collections and Legacy Points are account-wide across rulesets, with Hardcore as the exception: what you earn in Hardcore can become available elsewhere, but progress made elsewhere never flows into Hardcore. The PvP ruleset will carry faction-balance systems along the lines of Season of Discovery.

sources.label: PC Gamer, 10 big Forever details from BlizzCon

entries.title: Six new race and class combinations, with more planned.
entries.html:
The Deep Dive gave the full launch list: Gnome Priest, Human Hunter, Dwarf Shaman, Orc Mage, Troll Warlock and Undead Paladin. Blizzard says more are planned for future updates.

This supersedes announcement-day coverage, which had only Undead Paladin confirmed by cinematic and Dwarf Shaman reported from the demo floor. Night Elf Paladin belongs to retail Patch 12.2 and is not a Forever combination.

sources.label: PC Gamer, 10 big Forever details from BlizzCon

entries.title: Blizzard says the Skyborne are not a neutral race, and the two factions differ.
entries.html:
The announcement-day comparison to Pandaren was ours, not Blizzard’s. The panel transcript is explicit: “the Skyborne are not a neutral race. At character creation, players will choose whether their Skyborne joins the Horde or the Alliance.”

Horde-aligned Skyborne work with the Earthen Ring and gain Shaman; Alliance-aligned Skyborne work with the Kirin Tor and gain Mage. A demo transcription also records different second active racials for each: Skysight on the Horde side, Read Ley Line on the Alliance side.
entries.caveat: The faction-specific second racial comes from one demo transcription and is not in any Blizzard post.

entries.title: Dungeon drops grant their appearance to every eligible looter.
entries.html:
When a bind-on-pickup uncommon or rare item drops in a dungeon, its appearance is granted to every eligible looter, so nobody has to roll against an upgrade just to collect the look. Epic raid drops do not: only the player the item binds to gets the appearance.

Poor and common items grant their appearance as soon as they are looted, without binding. Armour type rules apply, so plate transmogs to plate and cloth to cloth, and low-level characters cannot use high-level appearances until 60, when level restrictions lift. PvP gear still requires its rank. Cosmetic-only items exist but will be rare.

entries.title: Transmog is opt-out, not opt-in: it is on by default and can be disabled.
entries.html:
This corrects what we published on 12 Sep. One outlet reported transmog as opt-in; Blizzard’s own Deep Dive recap describes a system that is on by default and can be turned off.

A mode selector appears the first time you log in, and choosing Classic Mode disables transmog automatically when you enter the world. You can change the setting later by talking to an NPC, and configure outfits at a transmogrifier in certain cities. Turning it off means you see everyone in the gear they are actually wearing.

With the system disabled you still collect appearances, you can still hide your own helm or cloak and display your own transmog, and you still see other players’ hidden helm and cloak settings.
entries.caveat: Supersedes the 12 Sep entry that recorded transmog as opt-in.

entries.title: Characters get two-part names, unique per region.
entries.html:
Because there are no realms to scope a name to, Forever characters have a first and a last name, and the pair is unique per region. Blizzard’s example is “Ana Forever.”

Players also choose a language preference at creation, which the game uses along with faction to lean toward grouping and phasing you with players who share it.

Blizzard frames two-part names as more room for an original name. Wowhead’s read of the same change is the opposite, that a region-wide namespace means more competition for any given name.

entries.title: Spell, melee and ranged hit become one stat, and so do crit; expertise is added.
entries.html:
Forever combines spell, melee and ranged hit chance into a single hit stat, and does the same for critical strike chance. Blizzard says this helps hybrids such as Retribution Paladins and Enhancement Shaman, and also makes Taunts, Poisons and Traps more reliable for Warriors, Hunters and Rogues.

A new stat reduces the chance for your attacks to be parried or dodged. Weapon skill still works the way it did, but individual items carry less of it so it is no longer the automatic best choice. Bonus healing now also carries one third as much bonus damage and appears on gear as early as level 10, and caster weapons grant spell damage and healing.

entries.title: Added reported level ranges for all nine new dungeons.
entries.noteAsBody: Reported by one outlet, not yet confirmed.

entries.title: Forever announced at BlizzCon. Beta 17 Sep, launch 4 Nov, level 60 forever.
entries.noteAsBody: Four new zones, nine dungeons, two raids, Darkspear Islands battleground, 1,000+ quests.

sources.label: Blizzard, World of Warcraft at BlizzCon 2026

entries.title: Skyborne Heroic Pack priced at $29.99, Epic Pack at $59.99.
entries.noteAsBody: Pack contents are from Blizzard's own post; the USD prices are press-reported and consistent across outlets, not stated verbatim in Blizzard's copy.

entries.title: Transmog reported as opt-in; disabling it shows everyone's real gear.
entries.noteAsBody: Reported from the What's Next panel by one outlet. Superseded on 13 Sep: Blizzard's own Deep Dive recap describes transmog as on by default and opt-out. Kept as a record of what was reported on the day.

about.title: About Forever Sixty
about.description: Who runs this site, how facts are checked, and how to help.
about.html:
Forever Sixty helps you play your class better in World of Warcraft: Forever. It is built and run by Commish LLC, an Arkansas company founded by players, and written and checked by players.

Every page says when it was last updated, under its title. Numbers come from the game client and our own sims.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard Entertainment. World of Warcraft and Warcraft are trademarks of Blizzard Entertainment, Inc. Forever Sixty is a registered trade name of Commish LLC. © Commish LLC.

To report an error, use Report a bug in the footer. To talk about a guide or offer to help write one, join the Discord from the footer.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What Forever Sixty collects, how it is used, and how long it is kept.
privacy.html:
What is collected

Your Battle.net sign-in identity; an email address only for an account first opened with the email sign-in link, which we no longer offer; combat logs and addon exports you upload; and, if you subscribe, a Stripe Customer id. We never collect, see, or store your card number, its expiry, or your CVC; Stripe holds all of that directly.

We count visits and clicks on our links without cookies or any personal data, and record which of our links, if any, an account first arrived from.

How Battle.net data is used

Anything sourced from Blizzard’s Developer API is kept for at most thirty days, per Blizzard’s own Developer API Terms of Use, and is never sold or placed behind a paywall.

Stripe

Stripe is our payment processor. Checkout and the billing portal are hosted by Stripe; see Stripe’s own privacy policy for what Stripe itself collects during that process.

Log coach

When a Premium player or an officer opens a coach review, one fight's numbers (spec, class, role, boss, raid size, kill or wipe, duration, level and the spells cast) are sent through the Vercel AI Gateway, which keeps nothing, to DeepSeek, which writes the review. It carries no character name, account, guild, realm or Battle.net data. What DeepSeek keeps, and whether it trains on it, is set by its Open Platform terms and privacy policy, and we do not control that. If the model is switched off, reviews fall back to the log-only text. Anonymising your account in its settings does not turn this off: a review is written when you, one of your guild's officers or a site moderator opens it, and anonymising stops only the moderator.

  • Vercel AI Gateway data retention
  • DeepSeek Open Platform terms
  • DeepSeek privacy policy

Cookies

fs_session and fs_csrf are functional cookies only: they keep you signed in and protect state-changing requests. There are no tracking or advertising cookies.

Data retention

Uploaded combat logs, the reports parsed from them, saved sims and the ratings derived from them are kept until you delete them or your account; the rankings and a character’s history are built from that record and would be wrong without it. Session rows expire with the session. If a storage limit ever becomes necessary it will be announced on the changelog with dates before anything is removed.

When you delete your account, it is gone at once: your BattleTag, email and Battle.net sign-in, every signed-in browser, companion and app, your Discord link and Premium role, your notification settings and watch list, your private reports, saved sims, addon exports and characters known only from your addon, and your guild memberships, applications and raid sign-ups. Any Premium subscription is cancelled at once, with no automatic refund; the refund policy applies. Only this is kept:

  • Stripe billing records, kept at Stripe for tax and legal reasons, with our link to them removed.
  • Public, unlisted and guild reports, with you removed as the uploader.
  • Character data from public sources, such as Battle.net public profiles and public logs, no longer linked to you. Battle.net data still ages out within thirty days, as above.
  • Builds you shared, as anonymous links.

Who is responsible

This service is operated by Commish LLC d/b/a Forever Sixty, an Arkansas limited liability company, which is the party responsible for the data described on this page. Mail reaches it at Commish LLC, c/o Northwest Registered Agent, LLC, 701 South St., STE 100, Mountain Home, AR 72653, United States.

Requests and contact

To delete your account yourself, open Your account, choose Delete account and type your BattleTag to confirm; it is done at once, as described under Data retention. If the account holds a guild’s claim or pays for a guild’s plan, release that first; the page says how.

To see, export or correct what the site holds about you, or to have your account deleted for you instead, email help@foreversixty.gg from the address or Battle.net account the request is about. You get an answer within thirty days. Those rights are yours wherever you live. The site runs no advertising, sells no data and builds no profiles.

refunds.title: Refund policy
refunds.description: How refunds work and what happens to your subscription when one is issued.
refunds.html:
Asking for a refund

Email help@foreversixty.gg from the account the subscription is on and we will sort it out.

What happens to your subscription

When a refund is approved, the owner cancels the subscription by hand in the same step as issuing the refund, and access ends then.

Partial-period refunds

A subscription is paid up front for its period. Cancelling stops the renewal and your access runs to the end of the period you paid for; we do not refund part of a period. If something went wrong on our side (you were charged twice, or paid for something that did not work), email us and we will put it right.

Who processes the refund

Commish LLC d/b/a Forever Sixty, the Arkansas company that operates this service, issues the refund through Stripe to the card you paid with. Stripe’s own timing applies from there, usually five to ten business days.

terms.title: Subscription terms
terms.description: What Premium and the guild plan are, how billing works, and how to cancel.
terms.html:
What Premium and the guild plan are

Premium and the guild plan sell server compute and storage: running simulations on our servers, keeping raw logs and saved sims longer, and (for the guild plan) tools for a raid group. Nothing from Battle.net (your characters, your sign-in, anything the game itself tells us about you) is ever sold or gated behind a subscription.

Billing and auto-renewal

Premium is $6 a month or $50 a year; Guild is $15 a month or $150 a year; Raid guild is $25 a month or $250 a year. Founder prices apply until 6 January 2027, as stated on the pricing page. A subscription renews automatically at the end of each billing period until you cancel. Stripe processes every payment; we never see or store your card.

Cancelling

Cancelling stops the renewal and keeps your access through the end of the period you already paid for; a period is paid up front and is not refunded in part (see the refund policy). After that, the account works exactly like a free one; nothing is deleted.

Price changes

If a price changes, you are told before it affects you, and the new price applies only from your next renewal after that notice. Nothing you have already paid for is repriced.

Account termination for abuse

An account or guild found to be abusing the guild plan (for example, an inflated or fabricated roster meant to split one subscription among unrelated players) may have its entitlement revoked.

The company

This service is provided by Commish LLC d/b/a Forever Sixty: Commish LLC, an Arkansas limited liability company, doing business as Forever Sixty, a fictitious name registered in Arkansas.

  • Email: help@foreversixty.gg

These terms are governed by the laws of the State of Arkansas. Any dispute that cannot be settled by email is heard in the state or federal courts located in Arkansas.

Battle.net-sourced data

Battle.net-sourced data is never sold. Blizzard’s Developer API Terms of Use forbid paywalling data or features that come from their API.
